status: draft protocol; runner not implemented; nothing fitted
question: Does held-out LFCC + Swin performance still improve as training patients are added, within the existing ECGData folds?

base_protocol.note: Only the training patients change. Cache, windows, outer folds, test patients, architecture, optimizer, epochs and seeds are the frozen base settings.

subsampling.count_rule: n_c = max(2, ceil(fraction * N_c)), where N_c is the number of class-c training patients in that outer fold
subsampling.draw: for each (fold, class, replicate): sort training patient IDs, permute with numpy default_rng(subset_seed + 1000*replicate + 10*fold + class_index), take the first n_c
subsampling.replicate_seed_pairing: replicate r is fitted with initialization seed r, so spread across the three fits includes both subset and initialization variation
subsampling.windows: all windows (all leads and recordings) of every selected patient; none from unselected patients
subsampling.test_set: the full held-out outer fold, unchanged at every fraction

fitting.epochs: fixed 40 at every fraction, as in the base protocol; smaller subsets therefore receive fewer optimizer steps
fitting.fraction_1_0: reuse the 15 Swin and 5 logistic trials in results/ecgdata_lfcc_swin_v1 read-only, after verifying them against reports/ecgdata_lfcc_swin_v1/artifact_inventory.csv; never refit or modify them
fitting.no_tuning: no early stopping, architecture change or selection based on test predictions
fitting.device: Swin on the RTX 5070 with the base determinism settings; logistic on CPU

evaluation.primary: window_macro_f1 averaged over the three replicate fits, at each fraction

bootstrap.paired: same patient multiplicities across all fractions, arms and replicates in each draw
contrasts: Swin minus logistic at each fraction
bootstrap.scope: conditional on saved predictions; excludes retraining uncertainty beyond the three replicates

interpretation_rule.still_improving: primary 1.0 minus 0.75 macro-F1 difference > 0 and its 95% interval lower bound > 0
interpretation_rule.no_detectable_gain: 95% interval includes 0 and point estimate <= 0.01; reported as no detectable gain at this scale, not proof of a plateau

not_allowed: extrapolating accuracy to a specific larger cohort size
claiming that other sources or populations would behave the same

pre_run_checks: unit tests: subsets are nested, class minimums hold, selected patients never appear in the test fold, subset hashes are deterministic
normalizer and class weights are computed from the subset only
the 1.0 reuse path verifies all base-run hashes and writes nothing there
synthetic interrupted-fit recovery reproduces an uninterrupted fit
protected-file hashes identical before and after the run

execution.estimated_gpu_time: about 10-15 minutes, extrapolated from the base run's 407.6 s for 15 full-size fits; an estimate, not a measurement

limitations: the primary contrast adds only about 16 patients per fold, so its interval is likely wide and an inconclusive result is plausible
fixed epochs confound subset size with number of optimizer steps
only three subset draws per fraction
the 80-patient cohort has informed earlier decisions and confounds diagnosis with source database; the curve cannot show whether patients from new sources would help
